grades.reason: This is only a table of contents. It lists section titles, including stimecmp, but gives no information on how to configure or acknowledge a timer interrupt.

grades.quote: If the `stimecmp` (supervisor-mode timer compare) register is implemented, STIP is read-only in mip and reflects the supervisor-level timer interrupt signal resulting from stimecmp. This timer interrupt signal is cleared by writing `stimecmp` with a value greater than the current time value.
grades.reason: This passage explains how the supervisor timer interrupt works. mip.STIP is the pending bit and mie.STIE is the enable bit. When stimecmp is implemented, STIP is read-only and reflects the stimecmp signal. The interrupt is cleared (acknowledged) by writing stimecmp with a value greater than the current time. This covers the acknowledge part well. It covers configuration only partly, because it gives no full setup procedure.

grades.quote: This extension serves to provide supervisor mode with its own CSR-based timer interrupt facility that it can directly manage to provide its own timer service (in the form of having its own stimecmp register)
grades.reason: This is a high-level overview of the Sstc extension. It says supervisor mode gets its own stimecmp CSR (and VS-mode gets vstimecmp) for timer interrupts. That is useful background for configuring a timer. It does not say how to program the compare value or how to clear the interrupt after delivery.

The passage describes only the LoongArch Timer Identity (TID) register, which holds the timer number that RDTIME returns. It says nothing about enabling, configuring, or programming a timer interrupt, and nothing about acknowledging or clearing one after delivery.
